LESSON: ANGLES

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Geometry
Topic 3.2: Angles
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Angles, part of Geometry in Grade 6 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: Where can you use angles in real life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. discuss angles on a straight line using concrete objects that have straight edges,

2. draw a line that cuts the straight line to form an angle. Measure and write the size(s) of angles formed. Compare the sizes of angles with your classmates,

3. work out the sizes of various angles on a straight line,

4. practically establish the sum of angles in a triangle and rectangles using different objects in the environment,

5. identify and draw equilateral, right- angled and isosceles triangles using geometrical instruments,

6. practically establish the sum of the interior angles in a rectangle and triangle,

7. use geometrical instruments or digital resources to practise drawing different lines and angles.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. discuss angles on a straight line using concrete objects that have straight edges,
2. draw a line that cuts the straight line to form an angle. Measure and write the size(s) of angles formed. Compare the sizes of angles with your classmates,
3. work out the sizes of various angles on a straight line,
4. practically establish the sum of angles in a triangle and rectangles using different objects in the environment,
5. identify and draw equilateral, right- angled and isosceles triangles using geometrical instruments,
6. practically establish the sum of the interior angles in a rectangle and triangle,
7. use geometrical instruments or digital resources to practise drawing different lines and angles.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Angles together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Self-efficacy: Learner confidently and practically establishes sum of the interior angles in a rectangle and triangle.

Values:
Unity: Learner works harmoniously with others to compare the sizes of angles.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Learner practically establishes the sum of angles in a triangle and rectangles from different objects in the environment as

enhanced in Environmental education.

Link to other learning areas:

Learner draws lines and angles that can be used in drawing and painting in Creative Art.
